Fatshark straight up lied at advertising. A lot of promo material weapons or cosmetics are unobtainable in game at launch, ability to obtain premium currency through gameplay was removed (and they were sneaky enough to edit this out of the discord post right before release), the crafting system that was supposed to be ready on release was added several months later. Amount of content is still questionable, but much less so. Game currently features only 4 classes with 3 subclasses, making it 12 (opposed to 15 free classes V2 had on release) and amost every map in the game have a reused fragments of another map in that same location.

Plus, almost all weapons for 3/4 characters are literally the same weapons, every class have access to couple of unique items, but all generic rifles/axes/swords are the same for each class, diluting loot pool. Only Ogryn gets a full set of unique weapons, but then he have very limited options. Sadly, im not rewriting this, as FS added almost nothing new in weapon department in a year of work, and most described problems still apply. At least they reworked some weapons to stop being so bad. 

The game still reeks of "effective management", "players engagement" and "retention" a year later. Also, in game shop exploiting FOMO and does not allow you to buy items directly, instead forcing you to buy aquilas in packs and then spending aquilas on cosmetics. This is still true a year later, and it's becoming worse with introduction of "premium skins" that are just the most popular regiment like Steel . Do not support this BS, vote with your wallet. No skin in a game worth $10+. Also, just to give you insight, when initial backlash to MTX was addressed, they promised to add the 100 aquilas bundle, that would solve some problems with the shop.It was added, but it is hidden from the shop, and only shows when you try to purchase the item you missing 100 or less aquilas. Isn't that convenient, eh?

It initially had timers, which were removed after community backlash, but this is still exploiting FOMO, don't be fooled. Also, they added a "convenient" bundle to buy the most expensive skin sets with a direct price of ~10,5$ per skin (this is dinda funny, after initial negativiy the head of the studio said in the interview that they SIMPLY FORGOT to release this pack, of course, we totally believe this). For anything less than the most luxury pack you still need to sit in the shop with a calculator and try to figure out how much you want to spend and how much unused aquilas will be sitting in your inventory after you finished. And just to clarify - yes, the game is released in poor tech state, missing features, a lot of maps reuse assets (literally same parts of the levels but you move through them backwards), core mechanics didnt finished, but MTX shop is ready to use and spew 2 sets of skins and 2 hats for each class every week. Aldo adding, latest datamine showed around 150 entries with cash shop interface, including full sets, weapon skins and some separate pieces, so don't worry, Fatshark loaded this shop for the very long run. In the grim darkness of the 41st millennium, there are only games released a year too early. 

Darktide is one of the best looking, feeling and sounding interpretations of the Warhammer 40,000 universe that has ever been released. Yet, it came out clearly too early and had many bugs and a poor progression system, with an in-game shop prioritised over promised features. That being sad, 10 months post release and after many, many patches, including the recently released complete rework of the class talent tree, it finally feels like Darktide is where it should have been at launch. 

Darktide is incredibly fun to play, as you slaw hordes of heretics with probably the most satisfying horde combat in a game yet, with the incredible soundtrack playing over the carnage and a near perfect rendition of a hive city it is incredible. The melee is an upgrade on Vermintide 1 + 2s, the shooting thankfully also feels incredibly weighty (especially Ogre weapons or the bolt pistol and the depth of the new talent trees, coupled with so many new abilities add a lot of depth to the game, especially at higher levels. The missions also feel very distinct visually and whilst there are shared mechanics between some missions they never feel like a copy paste of each other, likely due to the AI director and diverse location themes. 

Whilst I now feel comfortable recommending Darktide as a very good horde shooter, £50 is a high asking price. I would still recommend picking it up on sale, as you will get much more bang for your buck. Equally, it's a game best enjoyed with friends. I am very excited for the future of Darktide, now that it has found its feet and going by their record I am sure Fatshark will only further enhance this game to be one of the best horde games ever, which it really has the potential to be.

I can no longer in good faith wait for the game to be improved.

WAIT TO BUY THIS GAME

I love this game, I really do. I'm a huge 40k nerd and love the setting, hell I even played VT2 and loved that. But there is no excuse for the game to be in the state its in, and you should wait for it to go on sale or avoid it entirely for 6 months - a year. Even at 40$ it's not worth the money, and here's why:

Terrible optimization
- Many players are incapable of running this game at acceptable frames if they're able to at all. It's not uncommon to see complaints of rigs capable of running much more graphically intensive games at well over a hundred FPS struggle to maintain 60 after decreasing resolutions and lowering settings. This isn't even mentioning how inconsistent it can be on lower end machines, from running better than several thousand dollar rigs, to locking up one's system entirely. Memory leaks, random client-side crashes, and inconsistent at best servers which have a nasty habit of disconnecting people at random times in matches or preventing people from even logging into the game to attempt to play. While its better than it was in the beta, it's still common enough to be a reoccurring complaint.

Missing Content and Micro-transactions
- While the game has released in a half finished state, not even having a fully functional crafting system which was a selling point of the game, one which has been walked back and clumsily so by the CM's from what was promised in marketing and hype vs what is being delivered (over the course of December if the updates are to be believed), the game has a fully functioning Micro transaction store which is several steps back from vermintide's system of buying cosmetics direct for cash. This one uses a premium currency, and had until very recently employed FOMO tactics by placing the MTX store on a weekly timer (the timer is no longer in the MTX store, though the stock has failed to refresh for some reason). I personally don't mind a MTX store, or premium currency, though I preferred VT's implementation. But having one implemented in the "Full Release" before the crafting system, full arsenal of promised weapons (some of which are in promotional trailers and on the box art and aren't in the game) and supposedly the other 3/4 of the game is a slap in the face.

Anti-Player Tactics:
- While many are split on the implementation of the Coherency mechanic present in Darktide, many of the "achievements" (penances) for character progression are designed in such a way that it encourages players to either completely subvert or nearly actively troll matches to accomplish them. Some can't be completed without a full stack of coordinated players, and while there should be rewards for difficult things, they should be for all those who participate in a difficult challenge, not a moderately interesting T-Shirt for one team member. There are many more balance, design, and account issues which contribute to this beyond in game achievements, and I suggest you peruse the forums for a more varied series of accounts on this like the lack of either any or commensurate reward for completing challenges, beating optional bosses, or completing secondary objectives and the absurdly designed loot/shop systems with completely RNG weapon selection and weapon stat/blessing rolls.

Balance and Jank
- The game's servers have severe issues with hit-reg, spawns are janky and inconsistent, dodges don't dodge they temporarily break tracking so even if you're far enough away from an enemy to watch them whiff their strike you'll take damage, dodging with a ranged weapon doesn't break tracking so you'll get hit regardless, key combat components don't function consistently (suppression, melee challenging shooters, dodging disablers, the "you're about to be hit from behind so you need to turn around/spidey sense" noise not triggering consistently, etc), the game will spawn enemies directly behind you after clearing areas allowing enemies to get free hits, weapons are under powered across the board which makes the few properly tuned weapons stand out like they're op juggernauts, many talents (perks/skills) are broken/worded poorly/don't function at all/ or are severely underwhelming, the Veteran class dominates the game as it is one of the most optimally tuned classes with a solid answer to everything despite being marketed as a back line "sharp shooter", Zealot and Psyker have been significantly nerfed since the Closed Beta Test, stagger from incoming toughness damage often puts players in a death spiral on higher difficulties due to it staggering your movement and preventing you from getting out of fire, **as of 12/15/20 zealot's ultimate has been fixed**, every class in the game barring ogryn can nuke elite enemies faster than the dedicated elite hunter (psyker), blessings and perks on weapons can be counter intuitive and useless (like a reload speed bonus on weapons that don't use ammo), and many many many more issues. I again suggest looking on the forums for a more complete understanding.

Zero Endgame or Story
- One of the game's marketing tactics was to advertise that Dan Abnett, writer of the critically acclaimed Gaunt's Ghost's and Eisenhorn 40k Book Series wrote the story for this game. Much like the rest of the game, most of the story is missing as well. While I won't spoil the little that is provided, it's fair to say that the development team got confused between implementing the story and implementing the story board, as (and I say this without hyperbole) have read sparknotes with more detail and complexity. If Dan Abnett wrote this, they must've stolen the basic outline he wrote on a coffee shop napkin and ran with it. Additionally, there is no reason to max level your character other than to unlock the whole talent tree. You get no higher drop chance for better weapons, there are no incentives other than money (which is plentiful) to complete more difficult missions, you get no special missions or new modifiers. The best you get are decorative cosmetics and some changed voicelines among ambient NPCs in the HUB area. Everything is designed around artificial player retention, and a level 30 player with 30 hours on a character, due to the RNG, may have the same gameplay benefits as a level 30 player with 300 hours, personal skill not withstanding. There are 5 difficulties and 13 maps (supposedly), many are thematically identical, and while 40k is supposed to be grim dark, the series has a wealth of environments to choose from, even in a hive city which could've been implemented to introduce meaningful variety.

The End
- I could keep writing reasons why you shouldn't buy this game, but I will not as many have done so before me already. The core gameplay loop is amazing, despite its flaws, and here in a year or so i'm sure it will polish out. But you shouldn't buy this game. Fat Shark already made two tide games, the second entry in the series being a prime example of a phenomenal change from bad to good as the team polished the game up significantly over the years. But all of that progress is gone, all of the strides they'd made with QOL and gameplay, balance, combat, communication, transparency, etc have all been washed away. Somehow being the third Tide title, they've taken 2 steps backwards and none forwards. The entire community is very confused as to how the game has turned out as it has, and the fumbling of the Community Managers with regard to responding to these questions and criticisms has done nothing but evaporate goodwill and seed doubt. Despite what Hedge (a prominent community manager) will tell you, this game is in Early Access, and if you've played it you know it, regardless of how fun and enjoyable it may be. The game is not finished, and even with it being as fun as it is, it's not worth 40$ by any stretch of the imagination. Buy it if you like fun early access games or being a beta tester, but if you want a polished product you'll be left wanting. I suggest checking back in a year.

I used RNG to determine whether my review of this game with RNG crafting, RNG upgrading system,  RNG weapon shop offers, RNG mission selection, RNG mission modifier selection and RNG mission completion reward would be negative or positive.
Note for future myself - buy Fatshark games at least one year after release. No exceptions.

Darktide is an absolutely fantastic horde combat game brought low by terrible design of it's progression and secondary systems. I'll be comparing to Vermintide 2 heavily here, because Fatshark seems to have learned basically nothing from their last release.

Combat: 
Combat is for the most part excellent, fans of Vermintide will be well at home. Notable is that combat feels much better than Vermintide and ranged combat is blended much more cleanly with melee combat. Overall I have few complaints, in fact I wish I could judge the game on combat alone, because if I could this review would be positive. There are a few issues, notable that class balance is very uneven; the Veteran excels at basically everything in the game(although notably, the Veteran was unplayable for three days after launch because of a game breaking bug), the Ogryn excels at horde control and close range combat, where the Psyker falls behind greatly at higher difficulties and the Zealot feels unfinished. Still, all the classes are enjoyable to play up to difficulty 3 out of 5 difficulties. 

The Music:
Five stars.

The visuals:
Five stars, but the game runs like shit for most people.

Level Variety: 
The first truly noticeable problem in Darktide is that, unlike Vermintide 2, nearly every level in Darktide looks the same. In fact, you may notice in doing a different level, it seems like you're going through parts of another level backwards. Yeah, it's because you are. There is heavy assest reuse in the fairly limited number of maps, with only two areas that I can meaningfully differentiate visually. There is a Throneside map that takes place in a noble area and a Desert map that takes place in, well, a desert. Everything else is the same mishmash of reused industrial hallways. There's set pieces here and there, and I can't really complain about authenticity, because the levels FEEL very 40k. But in VT2 I could immediately tell what level I was in almost all of the time. In Darktide entire rooms are reused completely. 

Stability:
Game crashes, a lot. More than the beta.

Progression: 
Folks familiar with these games will know that you don't just clear levels once, you clear levels to get gear which you use to tackle harder difficulties. This has been horribly botched. In Vermintide 2, you got a chest after every mission with three items in it, the quality of which were based on the difficulty you tackled, the amount of challenge items you brought back(scriptures and grimoires), the amount you explored(loot dice), and the amount of monstrosities you slew(loot dice), and some RNG. Good players could consistently get the highest end crates by tackling higher difficulties and coming back with 3 scriptures and 2 gimoires, a "full books" run. You were also awarded a chest whenever you gained enough experience for another level, even if you were at the level cap. If you didn't like the items, you could break them down into materials to craft items you did want to use; so if I kept getting blue swords, but I wanted a hammer, I could break down a couple blue swords and get enough materials to make a hammer of my level and upgrade it to a blue. Pretty clean, pretty satisfying, and doing missions was always rewarding since at the very least you were getting materials to upgrade your stuff or reroll perks. 

All of this is gone in Darktide. Monstrosities(boss monsters) do not drop loot dice, scriptures and grimoires grant a pathetic amount of XP for returning them(and grimoires are HARDER) when they even spawn in a level, and you only, very rarely, get a single item at the end of a mission whose quality seems completely detached from both the difficulty and the teams performance. So how does one get gear? The geniuses at fatshark have common up with an incredible idea: there's a gear shop with a completely random set of ~10 gear pieces that you can buy that resets hourly, conveniently located next to the real money cash shop, which you have to run past to check the gear store from the hub location. So yes, you will have to run past the cash shop after every other mission to check that maybe the gear shop has something you actually want. The best way to get gear you want is to leave the game open in the background(good luck, it's a resource hog) and check the shop every hour. 

Crafting new items of a type you might actually want is not in the game nor is it planned to be, and the community manager has called such a feature lore unfriendly; something which is absolutely not true if you are at all familiar with 40k lore. One of four planned crafting features exists in the full release of this game, which is the ability to upgrade gear a rarity tier in exchange for crafting materials found in missions. These upgraded items have random perks and blessings. Oh, and you have to run past the real money cash shop on the way from the gear store to the crafting shop. 

There is one other store for items, which sells stuff in exchange for a weekly currency you get from doing special contracts. These are fairly easy but this shop only resets daily with four higher quality items, but I've yet to see a weapon worth buying in it. The contracts deliver most of their value from completing a full weekly set of them, which is especially frustrating as the contracts often completely bug out and do not progress at all even when you fulfill their requirements. 

The Hub: 
It's bad. You know how the castle in VT2 loaded quickly and you could switch characters instantly? That takes two loading screens now, I assume because the hub is fully online. And I can't think of a single reason to make the hub a worse experience other than so that you'll look at other players cosmetics. VT2 had just your party in the hub and ran much better. There is a test room with every type of enemy in it now though, so I'll give them credit for that improvement. 

Microtranscations & Cosmetics:
I will note that Fatshark, as of 2021, is a subsidiary company of Tencent. If you aren't familiar with Tencent, they are a Chinese company infamous for pumping games full of microtranscations. I have no idea how much influence they have over Darktide's microtranscation model, but there's some predatory design in this game. 

As I've mentioned above, the cash shop is positioned so that you have to run past it constantly, and the hub is designed to get you to view other players cosmetics. There are some free cosmetics in the game, but these are either earned by ridiculously stupid challenges, like kill a monstrosity by doing 90% of the damage to it with a single class ability, or ending a mission with zero ammo and 100% accuracy on a class that regenerates ammo when it kills a special, or taking no melee damage for an entire run, or doing an entire run without ever being more than 10m from ANY of your allies. There are also some cosmetics you can buy with in game currency, but they are all recolors. The paid cosmetics are generally better looking, and Fatshark has implemented full FOMO by putting up 2 cosmetic sets each week for each class with no information on what will be coming next rotation or when the cosmetics currently in the shop will be available again. 

Fatshark & Broken Promises: 
Fatshark is a developer who, even prior to being acquired, had no idea what a timetable was, and often broke their game for months by introducing poorly planned features before going radio silent. This is on full display with this release. The full release of the game is missing advertised weapons, advertised cosmetics, and advertised progression features. I am fairly confident based on the lifecycle of VT2 that these things will be added; eventually. When Fatshark gets around to it. And when that happens this game will probably be worth your time and money. Until then? I'd give it a pass unless you really really love both 40k and VT2, and are willing to play a game that is much worse than VT2 just for the 40k aesthetic.

Alright Fatshark, you could have struck gold with this one. You had it handed to you. The setting, the previous experience making not one but two of these games already, you guys had this game in the bag from a conceptual standpoint already. But, you BLEW IT. Your core gameplay loop during missions is spot on, you nailed it. But you only gave us 4 maps to play on, and yes, there ARE different missions for those maps. But it's still the fucking same map, it all looks and feels the same most of the time. You just reversed the way you run the map. So who cares. 

At Vermintide 2's launch, we got 15 classes. Now you give us 4. FOUR. WHY FOUR. You're working with the 40k universe and you BARELY did anything with it in terms of classes. Why? Why so little when you could have done so much? It's disappointing to say the least. The Veteran goes PEW PEW and that's it. Great. Fantastic. 

This game is in no way as good as Vermintide 2. And what sucks is I wish it was. I really do, I was beyond hyped for this for months. 

As of this review you've had a 90% drop off rate of daily players from launch, get your shit together Fatshark. I'll see you in a year after you've fixed this bug fest.

Let me make it clear - the core gameplay is really fun when the game works. Combat is meaty and visceral and it feels amazing to play with your friends.

That said... nothing in this game is finished or works right and the developers are extremely dishonest and keep lying to the community constantly.

1. The game is very unstable. Crashes plague most players. If the game isn't crashing then you're getting vague error codes disconnecting you from matches (which is frustrating because you get no reward on loss), massive load times to get back in, and issues getting your group together.

2. The balance makes literally no sense. Damage numbers are apparently chosen at random for weapons and the modifiers from perks are equally arbitrary. The same tier of traits for you to choose from will have choices like: 5% more damage every 3rd strike, 5% damage reduction, or deal double damage for 10 seconds every kill. There is only one real choice.

3. The itemization, loot, and end game are not finished. The shop randomly generates 10 weapons every hour and you have the privilege to buy them. Most of the weapons are crap and have random rolls so you just have to wait for the next hour. You get no rewards for actually playing the game, playing well, and finishing missions. The game is just this shop.

4. There is no story in the game. The developers bragged about a complex and engaging story written by author Dan Abnett... there is no story in the game. There are 5 short cutscenes introducing vendors and that's all. The developers blatantly lied to the community.

5. Crafting isn't in the game even though it was advertised - along with weapon modification. The developer lied to the community saying it would be in on launch, then right after launch, then by the end of December... even though they knew all their staff was on vacation and not working on the game. You can't  trust anything they say.

6. The cash shop is predatory and insulting. It was the only thing that worked right on launch. And they had the gall to also make the offerings limited time only... and when players complained they said "we didn't want to confuse players with too much choice". Lie after lie and marketing lingo/buzzwords. The cash shop skins are also poorly made and have missing fingers when worn, clipping items, or don't animate properly.

7. The cash shop also makes you purchase a secondary currency instead of just spending money on Steam... and of course they don't actually sell the exact amount of currency you need to purchase anything.

The developers have had 0 transparency, insult the players, and in general treated the community very poorly. They've misrepresented their game and the games' content. I can not recommend this game to anyone that isn't the most staunch Warhammer 40K fan.

Prioritizing micro transactions before basic features that were previously available is not right and making it so you have to overspend to get the cosmetics you do want is a disgusting practice.

In-mission gameplay is fantastic. Some of the best visuals in a game I've seen, with amazing and detailed thematic environments, weapons and characters that bring 40k to life. 

This game has some of the best combat responsiveness in the modern gaming scene. You hit an enemy from any angle with force, they'll react from that hit based on the weapons weight by getting thrown aside (with multiple animations for this too). You hit an enemy with a laser gun it leaves burn marks, and cracked armour reveals their faces underneath. Your bullets whizz past an enemy, they'll flinch and try find cover. Lots of awesome gore too. 

Why the negative rating then? This game seriously lacks meaningful progression, and its launch was nothing short of terrible with horrible optimisation problems and even less things to do than there is now. The cosmetic shop is an insult, as players have already paid money for the product yet if you want these fantastic cosmetics the artists have made you need to spend more real money to get them rather than earning them by playing the game. 

I love this game and want to see it succeed, so here are my suggestions that I hope fatshark would consider:

Remove the level cap at 30, let us level indefinitely to show off dedication to a specific class with milestones rewards such as a bonus in gold, new player frame unlocks (which is a png, a team of artists could bash out 100 in a day easily). Add earn-able player titles which can be displayed after the players first name, this is a low effort addition which would let players customise themselves further and give more rewards to fill out these indefinite extra levels.  After a while there would be no rewards but it still is fulfilling to watch your player rank go up. 

Let us earn the premium currency with challenges. I understand the time needed to create brand new cosmetics (fresh new models and not re-skins) is a time consuming process. Let players who want to buy the skins outright do so, but also let players who don't want to buy them EARN them over a long period of time of just playing the game and doing fun weekly challenges to obtain them.

There needs to be a way to see our stats after games and in general, a weak argument was made by Fatshark that showing stats increases toxicity which is ridiculous as there will be toxic players regardless of any game and stats are so important for players to review if a build they've made is good or see if a new strategy is working well. Give us weapon stats, let us see how many enemies we've killed with our gun. You could even make this an obtainable upgrade from player levels which we can attach to guns we like to show off how many enemies we've slain.

A game with great potential and fantastic developers, thank you fatshark for bringing 40k to life and continuing to improve the game but please listen to your community. For people considering to buy it; Is it worth your £30? If you're happy to spend around 50-80 hours of gameplay before getting bored then I'd say it's worth it.

In September of 2024, the Unlocked & Loaded patch dropped for Darktide. This patch brought with it the long [i]long[/i] awaited itemization and crafting rework. It included features such as a mastery system to unlock weapon blessings and the removal of locks when crafting weapons. All of which, were fantastic additions to the game.

Having pre-ordered Darktide over 2 years ago in November of 2022, I have had the opportunity to experience how far the game has come. Unfortunately, this comes with the nagging realization of "Why did it take 2 years of development to get the game to a place that's worthwhile?"

Many of the features that have since been added over the years, have been incessantly clamoured for by the community. Sometimes, modders would take matters into their own hands and create those very same quality of life features that are now a part of the core game. For instance, the now obsolete Contracts Overlay mod, released on 2023-04-27, would allow you to pull up your contract progress mid-mission. It only took Fatshark an entire year to include a similar functionality with the Path of Redemption update (2024-04-16).

Something as simple as wanting to track the live progress of a grind during a mission, seems like a functionality that should have been included on release. In what scenario, would someone [b]not[/b] want to know that they've performed enough Scab melee kills and can now focus on Dreg ranged kills? Perhaps there's someone out there who enjoys inefficiently exceeding targets for no additional rewards /s.

Ultimately, there's a theme of basic quality of life features, that should've existed on release, being incorporated years later. Although some features, like NumericUI, are still awaiting an official Fatshark implementation (maybe in another 2 years?). It's all very disappointing and if it wasn't for modders, I would say that the gameplay experience would have been far worse off.

If someone were to ask me, whether I would recommend vanilla Darktide. I would say "No." for most of the game's lifespan. Only now with the Unlocked & Loaded update and the recent closing of the [url=https://old.reddit.com/r/DarkTide/comments/1gjq0v5/the_book_of_grudges_is_closed/]Book of Grudges[/url], do I feel like the game is worth recommending. But I can't lie, it's both a reluctant recommendation and a cautionary tale of the classic Fatshark development curse (it looks like the Vermintide veterans were right all along).

Well, I never bothered to write reviews until now so something went REALLY wrong here:

Just as everyone says the core gameplay is very fun and the level design can be gorgeous at times but that's about it with good things to say about this whole mess.

The game has great potential but is heavily slowed down by outright braindead and anti-customer decisions not to mention the blatant lying of Fatshark.

So what is wrong in particular? Here's a small list from the top of my head:

-a NON-EXISTENT crafting system that was announced back in December with the only options you have to date is to upgrade the rarity of an item or reroll one(!) stat which locks you out from rerolling another stat

-Dan Abnett was only used for hype generation since there is NO STORY to speak of

- completely random crashes and disconnects (fortunately mostly disconnects happen for me)

-mission breaking bugs i.e. mission events not triggering after pressing a button softlocking you and forcing you to forfeit mission rewards

-penances that essentially make you grief your team

-no end of mission scoreboard so no way of knowing how effective you were and where you could improve your build

-a perfectly functional and overpriced (one whole cosmetic set is about 8-10 bucks compared to VT2's 3-5 bucks) MTX shop with currency packs instead of direct purchases (where they also "forgot" to add a currency pack that actually fits a whole cosmetic set without wasting currency until later) and some skins not even made properly with some parts clipping or downright copypasting that is conveniently placed right next to the weapon shop

-the Hub area that forces you into a loading screen whenever you change your character with the SOLE purpose of showing you other players that might've bought a cool premium skin that You too might spend money on

-a character slot limit of 5 and only 4 classes available now reeks of "buy additional character slots for x amount of Chinabucks" when more classes are added into the game

-a whole month of complete radio silence just to release a corpo speak laden letter of hollow promises topped with hot air and indications of SEASONAL CONTENT of all things (as if players don't feel scammed already)

I have no idea which of these tactics are FS's idea and which are Tencent's but Darktide is a prime example how corporations are infecting and ruining the gaming industry in the past years.

I might pop in now and then for a mission or two whenever I might feel like it but I've learned not to trust any hype before anything is released.

In conclusion: it's only a hair's breadth short of a complete scam. Don't buy until either heavily discounted or the issues are seriously worked on.

It's sad how corporate decisons ruined a potentially great game. Until these issues are not adressed I won't change this review.

I've played this game since the Beta. I loved this game, despite it's flaws and false promises. I eventually got kind of bored because there's no real updates that add anything, only ones that feel like they take from you. A portion of the community exploded around january/february, and I thought it was silly. I don't, anymore. Fatshark has decided it's a brilliant idea to just keep nerfing majority of things while buffing a small amount here and there. The most recent update has actively wasted my time. This game features RNG weapons and stat boosters, with randomized weapon stats and effects. I spent the better part of 3 weeks to get enough resources (and the weapons themselves) to upgrade weapons I enjoyed playing to be as good as I could get them for 3 weeks worth of resources. This most recent update has gutted them, and the weapons that weren't effected have lost their place in my load out because of it. In a PvE game, they are actively weakening the more commonly used weapons, while leaving the ones that don't get a lot of play due to under-performance still weak and useless. They feature a shop that has microtransactions, and up until relatively recently that was getting the main focus. Now, it hasn't been updated since they're focusing on ruining the other aspects of this game. There are only a handful of cosmetic items you can unlock through gameplay, and in many cases the sheer dedication it takes to unlock them via the unrealistic and arduous challenge to get them isn't worth the time and frustration. Crafting was promised, but not implemented. When it was, everything was insanely expensive to make with in-game resources. And with frequent nerfing and RNG being the only way to get them, it isn't worth it either. This game could have been fantastic, and I did admittedly enjoy much of the time I put in. But this last grind was made pointless by terrible updates that are truly tonedeaf and come across as the devs not playing their own game, or having any foresight, caution, or care in what they subject their player base to. Do you love 40k? Me too. Do you like horde shooters? Me too! Do you think they'd work well together? Of course they would, but not with this team behind it. Do not waste your money, or your time. The Devs will make sure both are wasted. Sadly, avoid this title. If you find classes and weapons you like, I assure you it's only a matter of time until they decide to make it so you won't.

Update: They have revamped the class system to offer more customization in play style. Each class has 3 trees that you can mix and match, and in my opinion has given more variety to the gameplay. Some of the weapons are still meh, but it's I think it's fair to say they're making a more concerted effort to try to improve the game. I've put another hundred hours in at the time of this update, and I have been enjoying myself. I am getting to the point where I'm growing tired again, but I felt it was only fair to keep honest with my review. I wish there was a more neutral recommendation, because I can't say I'd recommend this to everyone, although I do think it's worth trying out. Also, nailing a charging mutant with a rock as an ogryn and watching them break the sound barrier as they ragdoll is never not fun.
Weirdly relaxing game. You get into a sort of zen rhythm and just chill your way through it.

This is FatShark's third game of the "-tide" series.
You'd expect there to be improvements over the last 2 iterations, especially if the community has given the devs ample feedback over the last 7 years.
Unfortunately, it feels like this game does not only lack any improvements, it has actually regressed on several fronts when compared to its predecessors:

-Missing core features (crafting sytem, some of the  promised 70+ weapons are missing, same for the cosmetics shown on the cover of the game).

-Poor performance

-Poor netcode (esp. on higher difficulties, the more enemies, the worse it gets)

-MTX shop at launch that preys on FOMO and only offers ingame currency packs that do not match ingame prices => always a bit too much or too little currency to buy stuff.
Additionally, the MTX shop is the only place for new cosmetics. The "regular" ingame store only sells recolored versions of the base game cosmetics. Even cosmetics as minor as a cap or bandana are not available in the "regular" store and can only be bought with real money. 
Oh, and don't expect there to be any decent cosmetics that can be earned ingame, it's literally a F2P cash shop in a $40 title, 90% of cosmetics can only be bought with real money - even basic cosmetic items are cash only, e.g. a simple bandana costs ~$4!

-Core gameplay is great and enjoyable but a far cry from the smoothness of Vermintide 2, it feels like all the refinement Vermintide 2 got over the years is completely missing and we are starting from scratch. 
Weird design decisions that had already been solved in Vt2 have been reintroduced, like enemy icescating, chargers being able to do 90° turns on a dime, facespawning enemies or enemies spawning right next to you in one of the "clown closets", so you can have a full wave of specials and a horde pop out of a tiny door right next to you with no warning.

-Poor balance as of right now.

-Atrocious grind to max out the 4 classes (~20-30 hours per class).

-Even worse grind to get endgame items and resources: layers upon layers of rng mechanics with little to no player agency. Endgame item grind is just playing a slot machine with a painfully slow grind for each gambling attempt. 

-The best part? The above grind for items and resources is not account-wide! You get to grind weeklies, resources, items on all of your characters seperately because nothing is shared between them (some weekly quests can take ~6-10 hours, and you get to do it 4 times over, or maybe you get an item that'd be awesome on your zealot but unfortunately you got it while playing veteran, so your zealot can't use it all).

-All in all just chock-full of anti consumer practices that do not respect the player's time. The progression system in this game is really poor. It is 100% designed to artificially increase playtime because otherwise there'd be content.

-Talking about content: you are not able to freely select the map, difficulty, or modifier you want to play. Instead, you have to hope that the rng map selection screen gives you the combo you want. 

-You can't even start a private game with solo or with bots, it's always public (edit: they added private games for parties of 2 or more players, so still no solo games with bots - not that you'd ever want to play with bots, they are worse than useless).

-Speaking of maps: they capture the look and feel of 40k quite well. 
Yet they get extremely repetitive and monotonous really fast. 
There are only 2 main themes for overall map design: dark metal hallway and sandy/rusty metal hallway. 
There are exceedingly few memorable places across all maps, 90% of all places are literally just "dark metal hallway".  
It's a shame that there is next to no variety. Even worse, maps blatantly reuse locations from other maps and it's not like the game makes up for that by having lots of different maps either.

-There is one aspect in which Darktide offers improvements over Vermintide 2, namely the ability to test weapons against live targets in a training environment (you still have to grind to level 30 to unlock all enemies for testing though).

In conclusion, I'd only recommend this game to people who are fully aware that they buying an Early Access title masquerading as a full release. 
Or you are desperate for a 40k game with good gameplay and do not mind the fact that everything besides said gameplay is riddled with anti consumer practices.
Otherwise, wait until the devs have actually finished the game and revamped some of the horrible design choices.

If this is your first "-tide" game, some of these issues might not impact you quite as much. 
Still, if you are looking for a Warhammer fix, get Vermintide 2, which is far more refined, is cheaper, has greatly more content, and significantly more QoL. 
Seriously, Vermintide 2 feels like the sequel to Darktide instead of the other way around.

Hi, this is my 100 hour review.

Good: Devs
Bad: Executives
Explanation: Visuals audio and gameplay are top notch. They nailed the 40k atmosphere, gunplay and melee are visceral and satisfying. The mission types are fun, there needs to be more of them however. 

The problems are things that happen outside of an actual match.

The crafting scheme is a huge middle finger from Fatshark/Tencent C-suite straight to the playerbase. The timegating, the arbitrary locks, the system of gaining blessings etc...all of this is aimed at artificially inflating play time, a ploy aimed at hiding Darktide's lack of mission content. This synergizes with a cosmetic shop that only rotates one page twice a month. So they keep a player stuck on a convoluted upgrade/crafting scheme so they can drip-feed overpriced cosmetics to them for as long as they can get away with.  Why else would the cosmetic shop rotate so slowly if not for weaponizing FOMO against you? For contrast, Vermintide 2 has all cosmetics available all of the time in the shop. You will also pay far less for a new class+cosmetics in V2 than you would for simply a cosmetic in Darktide. 

It almost seems as if Fatshark has forgotten all of the lessons they learned from Vermintide 2, unless of course, they are simply focused on squeezing their loyal fans for all they are worth. 

We are their lifeblood, perhaps we have all forgotten this?

The game gets a negative review for me. Darktide is an amazingly fun game that has been hamstrung by greedy Tencent overlords. If/when the crafting/shop/greed situation is addressed, this review will flip to positive in an instant.

UPDATE: So crafting has been changed dramatically, allowing a significant amount of increased freedom in how you built and improve your weapons. The list of changes on this front is massive, so I won't fully explain it here but suffice to say it's miles better than it used to be. You actually feel like you have control over your inventory now.

OLD REVIEW: I've been holding off & holding off on leaving a negative review for Darktide, in the hopes that Fatshark will finally get their act together and listen. After today's patch, they don't get any more leeway.

Look, the gameplay is great. The combat feels excellent. The art direction is fantastic. The soundtrack is killer. All the stuff everyone has already said before me. The issue is their management decisions focusing entirely on making things take as long as humanly possible without giving you enjoyable reasons to stick around.

Crafting is intentionally grindy, with gear options locked to only allow you to change half of the effects that are randomly assigned to it. On top of that, you have to wait & wait & *wait* for a good enough base weapon to invest your time in, only to have it roll two terrible Blessings and have your time wasted. Currency isn't shared between characters meaning if it takes you (and I'm being generous here) 100 hours to get your Veteran into a spot where you're at least satisfied with their gear, it'll take you another 100 hours to get your Zealot to the same place, and another 100 hours for your Psyker *and another 100 hours* for your Ogryn.

The mission selection is another time-waster. There are 16 playable missions on rotation at any one time, spread across all 5 difficulties. This means some maps are not in rotation when you want to play them. On top of that, missions have modifiers that add sub-objectives or raise/lower the difficulty by adding more enemies or changing how they spawn. These modifiers are *also* on rotation, so if you need to collect Scriptures or Grimoires for your weekly assignments (again, not shared across characters so you need to do 20 weeklies every week) you might have to play a difficulty that is way too easy just to grind them out (or worse, one that is too hard for you and means your team has to carry you). If you've played as much as I have, anything below difficulty 5 is boring. Difficulty 5 with Hi-Intensity is where veteran players get to really push themselves and test themselves against the worst the game has to offer... and most of them time it is out of rotation. The maps that are available are so overplayed that the community knows them by heart, adding to the grindy monotony.

Today's patch is emblematic of Fatshark's inability to adapt to what their players want. With all the issues listed above, they add a shop that adds extremely expensive recolours of old cosmetics (with in-game currency) and re-enable the FOMO rotation on their premium cosmetic shop. "But! They've added a new boss! And two new maps!", you say. The new boss is the Chaos Spawn from Vermintide 2 (their last game), which featured in the game's first cutscene so should have been in at release. Two new maps does sound great on paper, except one of them is locked behind their first community event in which the player base has to finish 900'000 missions to unlock it. And by unlock it I mean add it into the rotation so it *still* might not be playable, or might be playable but only on difficulty 3. Fatshark already know they've messed up on this front, as the mission total has come down from 1.4 million missions(!) since the first announcement.

Fatshark, I don't know what you're planning or thinking (largely because you refuse to let your Community Managers do that, despite them being good at their jobs), but you seriously need to take a look at what you have planned and think about how those plans are going to remedy the issues above. Then, give your CMs range to communicate these plans to the player base. Set reasonable goals and a roadmap and stick to it. Doesn't matter how long it takes to roll this stuff out, you've already trained your players on how to wait forever with no end in sight.

I've been looking for a worthy successor to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/550/Left_4_Dead_2/]Left 4 Dead 2[/url] for a very long time. My friends and I have played a bunch of co-op shooters such as [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/49520/Borderlands_2/]Borderlands 1&2[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/552500/Warhammer_Vermintide_2/]Vermintide 1&2[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1250/Killing_Floor/]Killing Floor[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/924970/Back_4_Blood/]Back 4 Blood[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/548430/Deep_Rock_Galactic/]Deep Rock Galactic[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/312670/Strange_Brigade/]Strange Brigade[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/218620/PAYDAY_2/]Payday 2[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/242760/The_Forest/]The Forest[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1085660/Destiny_2/]Destiny 2[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2183900/Warhammer_40000_Space_Marine_2/]Space Marine 2[/url] and more. It's a mixed bag, each title having its own strengths and weaknesses. But I feel like our quest has come to an end with Darktide as it raises the genre to a new level. 

The four keys of to great horde shooter are its gunplay, bestiary, level design and replay value. The devs of Darktide have made their homework and delivered above and beyond my expectations in all of these fields.

First, the combat system is brilliant. Melee no longer feels like a last resort solution and can be embraced as a primary role. The combat pace is intense, especially on high difficulty levels, however the action remains readable at all times. There's an outstanding variety of weapons and playstyles, from shovels and riot shields to flamethrowers and the iconic boltgun. They pack a punch and sound great. Successful hits are rewarded with satisfying VFX: bodies are torn apart by chainswords and explosive ammo, heads and limbs fly off, torrents of maggots flow out of dismembered plague cultists…

Talking about cultists, there's a decent roster of foes to be faced, each playing a different role in the field: disabler, area denier, damage dealer, armored tank, distractor… They'll put your target priorization, repositioning and dodging/parrying skills to the test. Each enemy type uses distinct barks and sound cues, and comes in two flavors for extra variety: Chaos Undivided and Nurgle.

The world of Darktide looks gorgeous in its own grimdark way. It isn't the great colorful outdoors paraded by vainglorious Space Marines, but an ageing, sprawling hive city similar to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1222370/Necromunda_Hired_Gun/]Necromunda[/url]. I wish there was a 'tourist mode' like [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/775430/Discovery_Tour_by_Assassins_Creed_Ancient_Egypt/]the discovery tour of Assassin's Creed[/url] so I could look around and enjoy the details, because missions require focusing full attention on combat. Level design is in the vein of Left 4 Dead: mostly linear and cleverly signed by lightning, though with more verticality. Mission completion typically requires between 20 and 40 minutes. There are currently 21 missions set on 8 maps, and after 120 hours of gameplay I start to wish there were more. Fortunately special conditions such as toxic fog or power outage can refresh the experience.

Action on screen is supported by a soundtrack full of bangers composed by Jesper Kyd. The resulting combo of ultraviolent gameplay and electro beats reminds me of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/219150/Hotline_Miami/]Hotline Miami[/url].

Replay value is provided by progression through the talent trees of each of the four classes, mastery of the arsenal of weapons, and the penance system which provides challenges and rewards. Exploring builds for my favorite class, the Veteran, has kept me busy since January.

Now a multiplayer game is only as good as its community. When my friends are unavailable for a private game I turn to the matchmaking system and play with randoms. So far I haven't had any bad experience. It's a Warhammer game but surprisingly there's none of the far-right nuts that unfortunately tend to hang around this community. People play the mission, help out each other (you have to if you want to succeed) and use the excellent pinging system and audio bindings to communicate. From time to time there's someone with an open mic urging the team to "get to the choppa" or whatever, but most runs are quiet, and voice chat can be disabled. It's worth noting that crossplay between Steam, PC Game Pass and Xbox is implemented.

Darktide has only a handful of weaknesses. Don't be misled by the character creation options: this isn't a RPG like [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2186680/Warhammer_40000_Rogue_Trader/]Rogue Trader[/url] but a pure action game with storytelling added as an afterthought. New content arrives at a rather slow pace: maybe two to three major updates per year. This doesn't stop Darktide from being a really solid shooter which I'm always happy to get back to when new maps or weapons become available.

edit: I nominate this game for the Labor of Love award 2024.

After the latest community update, where I was told that the reason for the shop rotation is to "avoid confusion" as if my smooth monkey brain melts out of my ears every time I enter a grocery store because there's just too many CHOICES, I'm finally going to bite the bullet and leave a negative review.

I really, really want to recommend this game, but ultimately, it simply isn't worth the $40 when compared to Vermintide 2. It's clear that the team behind this game has passion, and their community management is pretty much as good as it could possibly be for a release like this. They are slowly, painfully, attempting to move in the right direction with update after update. They clearly CARE. The problem is that the game is already out, and it's not broken, it's fundamentally incomplete. 

The game's "story" goes nowhere and resolves nothing, and none of the maps connect to each other in any way. Each of the four basic character types only has one subclass, when Vermintide started with five characters and three subclasses for each for a base total of fifteen (with more as DLC). Once you hit max level and deal with 5-star maps, there's nowhere to go and nothing to do. They added even higher-difficulty missions at max level, but they're still fundamentally the same pool of missions that you've always been doing, across the same pool of maps. There's no modding support (which Vermintide has always had), you can't actually pick what map you want to play (it's chosen at random from a pool), there are no user lobbies, just pure matchmaking that gives you much less control over what you want to play and how. You can't even play by yourself!

It doesn't matter how many balance changes they make or if they make achievements easier to get. It doesn't matter if they make the same maps even harder and restrict them to Level 30 players. It doesn't matter if they add the Chaos Spawn in from Vermintide or finally stop prioritizing paid cosmetics: The only way to fix an incomplete game is to complete it. I would suggest they do something like A Realm Reborn and fundamentally revamp the game from top to bottom. The only redeeming qualities this game has compared to its predecessors is that a) the core gameplay of shooting heretics is actually incredibly fun on its own, and b) it's legitimately one of the best depictions of an Imperial Hive city environment I've ever seen in a video game. It just needs a massive amount of work in every other area.

And I know I and everyone else keep harping on Vermintide 2, but even Fatshark seems to agree that Vermintide is the better product: They released a free three-map mini-campaign for that game a few months ago, complete with its own plotline, voice acting, and varied and interesting environments (it takes place in a wizard's tower and takes full advantage of it), while Darktide got a single map (that had to be "unlocked" with a half-baked community event), some modifiers to existing maps that can't be turned off, and yet more balance updates.

This isn't the act of a studio that's even remotely interested in giving its developers the resources to bring a floundering product up to par. To Fatshark, Vermintide clearly brings in more money and is complete enough that it can be given more complete updates with less work. So Vermintide will continue to receive support and Darktide will continue to starve until it dies from lack of player retention. And I feel really bad for saying this, because, again, the team behind this game seems to genuinely care about its success. Too bad it doesn't seem the bean counters do.

Warhammer 40,000: Darktide could be examined in a handful of different ways, and while I plan on going into most of them in this review, there is one that I will not. As someone who could not give a damn about the Warhammer 40,000 IP, world, board game, lore, etc. if I tried, I can not speak to how this game utilizes any of those elements. I will be discussing how Darktide functions as both a game and a piece of software, and anything else will be swiftly ignored.

Darktide is a class-based horde killing game from the same developers as Vermintide I & II. If you have played those games, you will know the vague idea of what you are getting into, but if you do not, I shall explain. 

Darktide is, if you wanted to oversimplify it, Vermintide but with guns. If you wanted to be WRONG, you would just call that description Left4Dead. Darktide takes inspiration from Left4Dead, yes, in a lot of ways, while also adding its own spin on game systems and mechanics. The ways in which it's similar to L4D are pretty apparent:

- You proceed through linear levels, with hordes of enemies to slash, bludgeon, shoot, and stab your way through. often to accomplish a certain task that varies per level.
- There is your typical variety of trash mob, with a surprisingly large amount of specialist and elite enemies to diversify your opposition, with a lot of overlap from L4D (Spitter = Pox Flamer, Witch = Demonhost, Charger = Mutant, etc).
- Witty Banter between player characters to add levity.

While this is all well and good, the ways in which it differs from other games in a similar genre is where the game truly shines, in my opinion. First and foremost is the fact that there is a class system. This means that each of the playable characters (4 base game, 3 purchasable DLC at present) have their own pool of exclusive weapons, skill-tree, and "role" in a team composition. There are numerous ways to build a character, and several niches that a player can fit into, depending on their playstyle and equipped weapon(s). I will give a brief overview on each of the 4 base game classes, with their strengths, weaknesses, and overall role here:

Veteran is your prototypical soldier class, with heavy emphasis on having your ranged weapon out and firing. On the surface, there isn't really a lot "special" about them, owing to their status as a pretty cookie-cutter dime-a-dozen soldier class, however they have a lot of hidden potential as a ranged cover-fire specialist and a support role in disguise. Ammo economy is a pretty big deal in Darktide, as you are stuck with the weapons you bring into the mission and maintaining your bullets and grenades is huge. Veteran has access to ammo-refund for laser weapons, auto-refilling grenades, a perk to allow your teammates to get grenades back from ammo crates, and a lot more. 

Zealot is a bit of a jack-of-all-trades class, and you never really know what you're going to get if paired with one. They could be invested heavily in one-shotting high-priority targets and dealing half-damage to bosses with their melee weapons. They could be specced into having a more support role with their Chorus ability, refilling the team's Toughness (Shield HP). They could be built as a pseudo-tank with Martyrdom and additional wound segments. They could be focused on trash clear with their signature flamethrower weapon and throwing knives. There are a lot of options with Zealot, and they are one of the most versatile classes in Darktide.

Psyker is the mage class, plain and simple. They are also the hardest class to play in the base game, owing to the way in which they use their psychic abilities and staffs. Any ability or weapon that uses their magic powers adds a percentage to their Peril meter, and if it gets to 100% full and you use a power after that, you go down and need to be revived. You can quell peril by holding the reload button, and it goes down slowly over time, and thus the push and pull of the class. High skill ceiling, high potential, high risk, high reward.

Ogryn is... hard to talk about. As the first class that I played, I have a soft spot in my heart for the slab, but if we are being honest, Ogryn is the worst DESIGNED classes in the game, base or DLC. It teaches new players a lot of bad habits, has a noticeable lack of weapon and build variety, and Slab's role in the team is, more often than not, just a one-note tank that doesn't have an X factor. Ogryn has two shotguns, one break action and one auto, two grenade launchers, two machine guns, and an assortment of sticks, some sharp, some blunt. There is a lot of redundancy in these offerings, both in their gameplay role, and in their "feel" as weapons. I have a lot of fun with Ogryn, but it is IN SPITE of the class and not BECAUSE of it. If you, like me, LOVE the "Big Man with Big Stick Do Big Damage" archetype, you will enjoy yourself, but do not be surprised if you run into trouble at some point in your playtime.

As a game, that's about as far as I will get into in this review. Now, as a piece of software, Darktide has its own set of issues. As someone who (sadly) is on Intel/Nvidia, I have not had any real issues out of the ordinary, however I have heard that on AMD, this game's performance is atrociously awful. Like, inexcusably so. There have been forum posts, discord threads, steam discussions all about it, and I would be doing this review a disservice if I didn't at least mention it. Piece of advice if you are on AMD would be to pick it up on sale, play a mission, and if your rig can't handle it, refund it. There are a lot of other details I could go into, but for the sake of brevity I will not. As a game, Darktide is quite a bit of fun, owing to its many builds and playstyles. Is it perfect? Far from. Is it more fun with friends? Yes, but so is everything else. Can it be frustrating? Sure, especially if the game keeps throwing Vanguards and Poxbursters at you until you Alt-F4. This is my third most played game on Steam. I greatly enjoyed my time playing it, the gameplay loop during missions is fun and engaging, the enemies are almost all extremely readable and fair to fight, you have agency in how you act moment to moment, and crafting problems aside I like that most weapons and skill combos can be viable if you have the skills and know-how to back it up.

All of this being said, do not buy this game. It is only complete in it's desire to wring time and money from you.

The game famously launched with a primary feature, weapon crafting, entirely missing. When it was eventually released, it was done in a way to remove as much agency from it as possible, with limits on how much it can be used and the resources to do anything being hefty (especially if you don't desire playing on the hardest difficulty, Damnation). As someone who had the time and dedication to live with and use that crafting daily, it was still a massive slap in the face and required sometimes several games to simply have another chance to buy yet another autogun that would get sold for a fraction of the value I put into it.

1.5 years after launch, the devs are now promoting that the crafting with be made better in a later patch. Unless the changes basically amount to a total rework and it ALSO somehow reimburses me for all the time and energy I wasted on a system meant to produce that waste, it will be too little to late.

The next patch as of writing is going to change the penence system to act as a battle pass. No new maps, stories, or even an overarching plot. Just a battle pass. I am genuinely insulted that after a year and a half of playing this "live service", it is going to give me another bar with boring rewards to encourage "retention" instead of just giving me a new place to fight or a new faction to fight, more classes, anything.

The story as well is completely missing. There is no relation between any map but the 2 most recent additions, and no sense of progression in your efforts within the game as a whole. Not even a passing remark of previous objectives or what your character has done. If you made a brand new character for every mission you ever did, it would feel identical as you bringing your level 30 character who has already killed thousands of pox-walkers over their career. I myself can look past that to an extent but somehow Darktide has managed to make me frustrated with this lack of presence we have within the "plot". 

I loved playing this game; honestly, warts and all. But it has demonstrated that it will keep spinning its wheels and wasting my time and pretend like it's going somewhere. And I cannot recommend you touch it unless the literal WHOLE game changes to fix these issues.
I absolutely abhor the FOMO stupid expensive cosmetic nonsense but the game itself is *FANTASTIC*. Visceral, exciting, a masterclass in environmental design and an absolutely banging soundtrack.
This game should be in early access. Frankly I'm shocked a company would release a game that is so rushed and still put in a cash shop.

Summary for this game is very mixed. as you can tell by the time invested, I'm thoroughly addicted to this game, and that's with good reason. But man oh man. It's a love hate relationship at this point.

You already know the deets, like the extremely satisfying combat, the top tier melee system, the banger ass soundtrack, y'know. When all the stars align and you're in rhythm with the game, it's very easy to look at the clock and be like "it's already 3am?". It's boatloads of fun with friends, and it's extremely satisfying making builds you enjoy and goring heretics with relentless fervour.

That's not why I'm leaving a negative review, though.

1. Constant framerate drops. Fine when there's not much on screen. Borderline unplayable when it dips to 20 FPS. Gets worse with every single update Big Fish spits out. I'm not running a build worth as much as someone's left nut, but you'd expect better on LOW settings with a 7900 XTX.
2. Crashes, crashes, crashes. Oh boy. It makes Saints Row 2 look stable by comparison. Mods or no mods, you will suffer, and it always seems to happen at the worst of times. On the Havoc challenge mode, this is downright rage inducing, as one teammate being missing is enough to completely tank your run. Aaand... you get punished for it.
3. Disconnects. You'll randomly rubberband, and get sent back to the character select screen because their servers are absolutely terrible. It's admissible if this is a rare occurrence. It is not. It's honestly EXPECTED at this point.
4. Bugs and glitches. Yeah. Joining a game in progress sometimes throws you off the map and kills you. The hitboxes for the rejects are inexplicably larger at this moment, you'll find yourself saying "How did that hit me?" on the daily. Any time a few bugs are fixed, Humongous Salmon will find a way to break something else, which is par for the course.
5. Questionable design decisions; power creep. The cycle never stops. Everyone uses a meta build, meta build too strong, so they inadvertently buff a bunch of stuff and forget half of the old content. How about armor literally cucking half the weapon roster? The largest normal threat are crushers, and they have no weak-points. Why? Taking off meta builds is treated like griefing in higher levels of gameplay, which seriously limits your choices.

I'd definitely take a closer look at all of these flaws, and dive into some research before getting hooked like I did. For now, I'm going to go back to saying I won't play this game, and end up playing it for twelve hours straight because I'm addicted to the core gameplay loop, while ranting about these issues the whole time. It's rather unfortunate, because underneath all of the graphical gripes and questionable update decisions is one of the most competent horde shooters this genre has to offer. I just wish Steam had the option to leave 'Mixed' reviews.

[h3]After 800 hours, Darktide is one of the best cooperative horde games I've ever played, and it's not even close.[/h3]

Darktide has had its bumps here and there throughout the time its existed. I basically skipped on the first year of the game due to the complaints I heard on it. Progression was bad, and the lack of maps made playing the same missions over and over lackluster. The lack of player agency in improving your weapons also made it a slot machine- a slot machine that'd be the [i]only[/i] thing you had to engage with. 

The main thing that has kept this game going, and what got me into it and still playing it, is the gameplay. GOODNESS, the gameplay! This game's combat is simple at its core, but every block and dodge and hit and ability feels worthwhile and engaging. No game has engaged me as much as Darktide, where I feel like everything I'm doing is meaty and worthwhile. Going from regular Malices to Auric Damnations then going back, and noticing how you're not even struggling instantly showcases just how better [i]you, the player,[/i] have gotten at the game. Team composition matters but its not instant lose if you have weird comps (like an all Ogryn squad: Tha Emprah protec's the lil'uns!) I have played this game with both friends and pubs, and both were enjoyable experiences, which is not something I'd say for many horde cooperative games.

The sound design of the game is second to none, with sound cues telling you when a trapper or bomber spawns, indicating that you need to deal with it. The whooshing sound of enemies about to hit you in the back, or a Mauler preparing for a nasty overhead that'll knock your karking ass to the floor; it is godly! And the same applies to your own weapons as well- the fact Fatshark got a Lasgun to sound chunky and not just another generic Sci-fi laser pistol should be credited, and all the weapons sound like they're designed to kill. That's not to discredit the music either; Jesper Kyd has designed a wonderful soundtrack for a setting where church hymns are what's considered "music" and flipped the whole thing on its head; it really sounds like you're going feet first into a slaughterhouse, which compliments the gameplay really well.

So, why'd I wait so long to review it? Well, I didn't feel comfortable to, until the most recent update: unlocked and loaded has made this game so, so, SO much better. Every problem I had with this game's progression just seemingly faded away. Where before I had to deal with subpar weapons or waste a ton of resources on what was essentially a slot machine, instead I could find a weapon who's stat distribution I liked, upgrade it, and make it immediately a meta weapon. No longer am I limited by my equipment; its all on how good me and the team is. I also don't want to discredit the previous Path of Redemption update; that Update introduced a ton of penances which helped me explore builds I never did before, and really helped me engage with some abilities I never tried before (Smoke grenades still need a rework,  Fatshark!)

Overall, I will say that yes, this game has issues. This game could still use more maps, more bosses, more weapons (especially for the gruttin' Ogryns!) and a different enemy faction. The story for this game is... not there. Certain audio bugs  can really be a downer when you go down because you couldn't hear a trapper or poxburster. But right now? This is where Darktide should've been two years ago: a good fun game where you can hop in, with weapons you built with a class and build you want to run, and just kill some heretics!

As of the end of the pre-release beta, Darktide is a mixture of both the best and worst parts of the Vermintide experience.

Crashes are common enough to be frustrating, the game play loop is repetitive and lacks the story progression and character of Vermintide and there are still a large number of basic mechanics that feel under-explained and poorly implemented.

But heck if it isn't the most fun I've had playing with friends in a while and it's one of the most aesthetically on point 40k games in years.

Fatshark clearly spent a lot of time trying to get the feel of a 40k Hive World down and it has definitely paid off. It's dark, unforgiving and brutal. Noises echo off the steel walls just right and every gun is absolutely perfect. The banter and world-building from Vermintide that was so excellent and such a big draw to the game returns in spades.

The gameplay itself reflects that as well. It's not just "Vermintide but with guns". There is a distinctly different feel, even playing as a tanky Ogryn. It's not genre-defining different or anything, but being able to mow down entire hordes with a Heavy Stubber feels intensely satisfying in a similar, yet distinct, way to how making Skaven fly for miles on the end of a hammer blow does in Vermintide.

Basically, this game is all about feeling. You will know whether you like this game pretty fast and if you do, you'll have a great time regardless of any of the issues. But if you don't get that feel, if it doesn't click, you're gonna really notice the VERY rough edges this game still has and it's not going to feel worth the asking price.

So can I recommend the game? If you like 40k, it aesthetic, it's soundscape, it's world, yes absolutely. If you're looking for a fun co-op horde game that's stable and has an interesting meta-progression an gameplay loop? Get Vermintide and wait a couple of years for this game to [i] become [/i] as good as Vermintide. Because it will eventually, but it's not there yet.

I cannot recommend this game in its current state.

Only one thing in the game is done right and that is the combat mechanics. 
Heretic slaying has never been so well done, which is why I still play this game from time to time and will continue to do so.

Now to the bad stuff:
- The equipment shop is hidden behind time limits. Forcing you to check every hour to see if a weapon with good basic stats has appeared, which is likely to turn into useless trash as crafting in this game is a joke.

- Crafting is practically non-existent, we only have stub options marked "coming soon". You can improve the rarity of a weapon or accessory, after which it has extra perks and blessings. Weapons have two perks and two blessings, of which only 1 perk can be rerolled. Two useless perks? Trash. Two blessings don't fit the build criteria either, so... also trash. Accessories have 1 blessing and 3 perks, and follow the same pattern as weapons.

- No variety of weapons, class is tied to one or two weapons in both melee and ranged combat. Speaking solely on behalf of the psyker. 4 types of staffs, 3 of which have practical use, but Trauma staff needs improvement. Close combat, the choice is simple - a power sword, with blessing to deflect bullets or any non-force weapon.

- No story campaign, not a problem for me personally. I don't play PvE horde shooters for the sake of story, but it was advertised and noted that Dan Abnett wrote it.

- A set of random missions, each has a specific timer, then changes to something else with or without other modifiers.
Just a pain in the ass if you say you need to complete a contract for 6 successful extra missions on a particular map, which may not drop for hours.
There's not much variation, we have about 5-6 maps that are used backwards in other missions.

- At first glance, not a bad system of extra modifiers, designed to diversify the small number of maps. Stopped working before the end of December. The timers for changing them are gone, and only increased/reduced number of specialists and enemies or increased number of pox hounds are left. No lights and purging ventilation, just gone.

- No stats at the end of the match. You can't tell how effective your loadout is, you can't tell if your stats are improving or not. Just like there is no understanding how well your team played, where you were weak and where you should have improved. Were you lacking in crowd control? or maybe you were ineffective in dealing with specialists and elite enemies.

- Cosmetic shop. While I don't mind the developers making extra profit for the cosmetics, it's done as poorly as possible here.
You can not buy directly, only through the padding in the form of special currency, which is sold by certain bundles.
Lack of normal non-paying cosmetics, except for various recolors, which are sold by the vendor equipment. It was very funny when the game wouldn't let me go further than trying to log in as a character, but still perfectly capable of logging into the cosmetics shop and making a purchase. Immediately you can see the main focus of the team, what's important and what's not.

- The performance is simply abysmal. I can't get a stable 60 fps without dlss even at 1080p, without the game turning into a mishmash of pixels on the screen. I have Ryzen 7 2700, 16Gb 3200hz RAM, RTX 2070S. Running game on ssd on medium settings without RT. Going all on low does nothing at all, at high i lose around 5-10 fps compared to medium.

- Weekly contracts. Pointless and useless, the same trash weapons and accessories, and the ability to re-roll tasks only 3 times.

The list could go on and on, but why? Too much is wrong with this game. Simple fixes are hardly helpful here, a lot of things feel like they need to be done from scratch. 
I regret that I decided to support Fatshark and bought the Imperial Edition. But there's still something about this game that appeals to me, and I'd like to see this mess cleaned up.

I'll continue to play from time to time, but I'll hardly change the review to "recommend" even if all the problems are fixed.
Emperor help us all.
